notes: TWO templates, one persona. (1) `Kinetic Business by Windstream`, the gold layout: a three-column header/value pair, `Account number Telephone number Invoice date` on one line and the three values on the next, so one anchor yields three fields. (2) `Windstream Enterprise`, carried in `anchor_alts` on every selector: same three-column idea but the labels are stacked over TWO lines (`Account Invoice Total` / `Number Date Amount Due` / values), so nothing spells `Account Number` or `Total Amount Due` as a contiguous run and each alt anchors a header row read across instead. Its summary ladder is reworded throughout (`Previous Total`, `Payments Applied`, `New Charges - Due by <date>`, `TOTAL INVOICE AMOUNT`) and it prints no telephone number and no separate `Due date` label. The two vocabularies are disjoint, so an alt is unreachable on a Kinetic bill and a primary is unreachable on an Enterprise one; `tests/packs/test_windstream_enterprise_template.py` asserts that, because it is what makes one persona safe for both. The sole exception is the brand name, which is on both - which is why `remit_address` is the one selector ordered the other way round, Enterprise label first and the bare `WINDSTREAM` anchor demoted to the alt: as the primary it matched the word inside a sentence of portal boilerplate and returned a paragraph. `vendor_name` is read ONLY on the Enterprise template, and that asymmetry is the point. The Kinetic text layer breaks the brand mid-word (`Kinetic Business by Windstre am`), so no pattern can capture it and the pack's display-name table has to supply it; the Enterprise brand IS readable (`ATTN: Windstream Enterprise Services`, present natively and surviving OCR), so the selector reads it and `resolve_vendor_alias` leaves the printed value alone rather than overwriting it with the table's single Kinetic-oriented entry. Printed evidence wins where it exists; the table is for where the print is unreadable. Both still collapse to the one `windstream` canonical (F5). bill_to_name (Task 8): both templates print the customer name directly below a fixed boilerplate line in its own column, so plain near-anchor reaches it - Kinetic off the whole 'Website: kineticbusiness.com' line (top=107.26, name at top=127.14), Enterprise off 'Check here for change of address(note changes below)' (top=110.25, name at top=144.66), the same disjoint-vocabulary anchor_alts arrangement the rest of this persona uses. The anchor must cover the WHOLE Website line: 'Website:' alone leaves 'kineticbusiness.com' (x0=470.88, same row) as the region's first candidate. The pattern is a party-name SHAPE rather than 'text' or 'text_block' because neither named pattern serves both templates - measured on the real PDFs, 'text' returns Enterprise's stray 'Y' form marker (top=128.13, x0=335.00, the only word of that row inside near-anchor's x1=347) and 'text_block' bleeds Kinetic's PO BOX / DURANT lines into the name. An 'above-anchor' mirror of near-anchor would NOT have helped either template: the nearest label below a Kinetic name is 'Account Summary' 94pt down (69pt for the payment stub's copy), both far outside the 40pt reach, with the address block in between. The three OCR'd samples miss (OCR renders the anchors as "Website' kineticbusiness.com" and with an inserted space) and fall through to resolve_bill_to_alias's roster rung, unchanged from today.
